# Field Notes - A Column of Opinions

By H. Pell, occasional visitor to the Gretna Marsh Pilot. Published in the district almanac, March 2031. The publisher insists this column mixes the writer's opinions with a few checkable facts, and readers should keep the two apart.

## On elegance

The Aeris-M is the most elegant field instrument anyone has shipped this decade. That is my judgment, not a specification claim. Its frit turns drift management into something close to a craft, and I will defend that view in any pub in Alderbury.

## On the firmware panic

The January panic about firmware was overdone. The facts: firmware 4.2.1 was released on 2031-01-06, and the first drift observation was logged on 2031-01-09. In my opinion the nearness of those dates says nothing about cause - the specification itself says the drift is mechanical in origin, and the specification is right far more often than the pub is.

## On the distributor

Cobalt AgriSupply's 120-day service interval is reckless, in my opinion, for any site that reports to the Board. Their plus or minus 1.2 percent accuracy claim is a bench-room boast. Neither of those sentences is a fact; the controlling figures live in Revision 2 of the specification, and I have read them.

## On batteries

The HydraProbe-9 will outlast the Aeris-M on paper - ten years against five and a half - and paper is where I leave it, because the two products are not interchangeable and nobody at this site pretends otherwise.

## On paperwork

Thirty-eight probes across six plots, and every calibration logged within 24 hours. Those are facts from the site register. My opinion is that the register office runs the tightest ship in the province, and the inspector who quoted the superseded 30-minute cadence at us last quarter should be made to copy the glossary out by hand.
